item.title: NEW: N-able Confirms Server Breach Caused Email Security Service Outage
item.description:
Headline: N-able Confirms Server Breach Caused Email Security Service Outage

Summary:
N-able has confirmed a security incident involving unauthorized access to a server supporting its Mail Assure and SpamExperts hosted cloud platforms. The breach, which began on November 16, 2026, led to a multi-day service disruption across the Americas, Europe, and APAC. As a precaution, N-able disabled management interfaces, APIs, and quarantine access. While core email filtering remained operational, administrators were unable to manage the services. An investigation is ongoing to determine the attack vector and full impact, though N-able has stated there is currently no evidence of customer data compromise. This incident is reportedly separate from a recent vulnerability in its N-central RMM product.

Severity: High

Categories: Cyberattack, Data Breach, Cloud Security

Meta Description: N-able has confirmed a security breach involving unauthorized server access was the root cause of a multi-day outage for its Mail Assure and SpamExperts services.

item.title: NEW: Visa Confirms Third-Party Breach by 'n0n' Gang; Premium Data Leaked
item.description:
Headline: Visa Confirms Third-Party Breach by 'n0n' Gang; Premium Data Leaked

Summary:
Visa has confirmed a data breach originating from a third-party vendor in the Asia-Pacific region that managed loyalty programs. The incident was claimed by the 'n0n' ransomware group, which leaked data on November 19, 2026, allegedly affecting over 6,000 premium Visa cardholders. Visa asserts that its own systems were not compromised and no payment card numbers were exposed. The leaked data includes information about customer engagement with luxury dining programs, such as campaign names and event details. Security experts warn this information could be used for sophisticated phishing attacks against high-net-worth individuals.

Headline: Expedia Investigates Massive Data Breach Claimed by 'n0n' Gang

Summary:
Expedia Group is investigating a major data breach after the 'n0n' extortion group claimed to have stolen nearly a billion records through a supply chain attack. The attackers reportedly compromised a third-party data platform, Qubole, using a stolen vendor key to access Expedia's systems. The 'n0n' group alleges it exfiltrated data including 830 million loyalty records and 58 million traveler profiles. While Expedia has not verified the scope of the theft, it confirmed the access method and has engaged external experts. Customers are advised to change their passwords and watch for targeted phishing campaigns.

Summary:

Following the disclosure, a class-action lawsuit was filed against UCHealth on November 18, 2026, alleging failure to protect patient data and criticizing the nearly four-month delay in notifying victims, which may violate HIPAA's 60-day notification rule.

item.title: NEW: Critical 'Java4Shell' RCE Flaw (CVE-2026-114938) Hits OpenJDK
item.description:
Headline: Critical 'Java4Shell' RCE Flaw (CVE-2026-114938) Hits OpenJDK

Summary:
A critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability, dubbed 'Java4Shell' and tracked as CVE-2026-114938, has been disclosed in multiple versions of OpenJDK. The flaw, rated 8.1 CVSS, is a memory corruption bug in the hardware-accelerated Base64 decoder on modern x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI support. An unauthenticated attacker can trigger it by sending a crafted Base64 string, leading to an out-of-bounds heap write. Popular applications like Jira, Confluence, and Jenkins are affected. Patches are available, and organizations are urged to update their Java runtimes immediately.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Vulnerability, Patch Management

Meta Description: A critical remote code execution flaw, CVE-2026-114938 or 'Java4Shell,' affects OpenJDK. The 8.1 CVSS bug allows unauthenticated RCE. Patch now.

Article Slug: critical-java4shell-rce-flaw-cve-2026-114938-disclosed-in-openjdk

item.title: NEW: Microsoft's 'agent-framework' PyPI Package Hijacked to Steal Credentials
item.description:
Headline: Microsoft's 'agent-framework' PyPI Package Hijacked to Steal Credentials

Summary:
A supply chain attack compromised two versions of Microsoft's official 'agent-framework' package on the Python Package Index (PyPI). On November 17, 2026, malicious versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 were published, containing a credential-stealing payload. The malware, affecting a package with ~190,000 monthly downloads, was designed to harvest secrets from developer environments and CI/CD pipelines, including credentials for Azure, AWS, GitHub, Docker, and npm. The malicious code executed automatically via a .pth startup hook, making it highly evasive. The compromised packages have been removed, but developers are urged to rotate all potentially exposed secrets.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Supply Chain Attack, Malware, Cloud Security

Meta Description: Microsoft's 'agent-framework' PyPI package was compromised, with malicious versions published to steal developer and CI/CD credentials for Azure, AWS, and GitHub.

item.title: NEW: Leaked Cloud Keys on Docker Hub Exploited in Under 8 Seconds, Study Finds
item.description:
Headline: Leaked Cloud Keys on Docker Hub Exploited in Under 8 Seconds, Study Finds

Summary:
Research from Stony Brook University reveals a critical software supply chain risk: cloud credentials and API keys accidentally embedded in public Docker Hub images are being discovered and exploited by automated bots in as little as 7.86 seconds. The study, which planted honeypot keys, found that all AWS keys were abused within 15 minutes, with a median compromise time of 51 seconds. The 'ContainerBots' use static analysis to extract secrets from image layers without running the containers, bypassing many runtime defenses. The findings highlight the near-zero window developers have to remediate accidental secret exposure in public container registries.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Cloud Security, Supply Chain Attack, Threat Intelligence

Meta Description: A Stony Brook University study shows automated bots exploit cloud keys in public Docker Hub images in seconds, highlighting a major software supply chain vulnerability.

item.title: NEW: Decade-Old 'nginx2root' Flaw (CVE-2026-123007) Allows RCE on NGINX Servers
item.description:
Headline: Decade-Old 'nginx2root' Flaw (CVE-2026-123007) Allows RCE on NGINX Servers

Summary:
A critical, decade-old remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in NGINX's HTTP/2 implementation has been disclosed. Dubbed 'nginx2root' and tracked as CVE-2026-123007, the flaw allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute code on vulnerable servers. It affects all open-source NGINX versions from 1.9.5 (released in 2015) to 1.31.8. While the exploit grants code execution as the NGINX worker process, it can be chained with a kernel privilege escalation to gain full root access. F5 has released patched versions. Exploitation is considered difficult, requiring large amounts of traffic, and no in-the-wild attacks have been observed yet.

Severity: High

Categories: Vulnerability, Patch Management

Meta Description: A critical, decade-old RCE vulnerability in NGINX (CVE-2026-123007) affecting the HTTP/2 module has been disclosed. Patches are available from F5.

Article Slug: decade-old-nginx2root-flaw-cve-2026-123007-allows-rce-on-nginx-servers

item.description:
Headline: Optimizely Supply Chain Attack Hits 178 Major Websites with Malware

Summary:
A major supply chain attack on the web experimentation platform Optimizely led to malicious JavaScript being served to visitors of 178 high-profile websites, including the BBC, CNN, Zoom, and HSBC. Discovered on November 16, 2026, attackers exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely's platform to inject a multi-purpose malware payload. The script, served from Optimizely's own CDN, was capable of skimming payment cards, swapping cryptocurrency wallet addresses, stealing cookies, and redirecting older iOS devices to exploit kits. Optimizely has since contained the incident by blocking the access path and removing the malicious code.

Severity: Critical

Meta Description: A supply chain attack on Optimizely compromised 178 websites, including CNN and BBC, serving malware that skimmed credit cards and stole cryptocurrency.

item.title: NEW: Over Half of Mobile Banking Apps Have Critical Flaws, Study Finds
item.description:
Headline: Over Half of Mobile Banking Apps Have Critical Flaws, Study Finds

Summary:
A security analysis of 2,686 mobile banking apps from 487 banks across 64 countries found that over 51% contain high or critical severity vulnerabilities. The study, by Ostorlab, identified significant risks including hardcoded credentials in 20% of apps, bypassable biometric authentication in 35% of Android apps, and the use of outdated, vulnerable components in 41% of apps. The research highlights a slow adoption of modern security practices like passkeys and underscores the systemic risk to global financial customers from inadequately secured mobile applications.

Severity: High

Categories: Mobile Security, Vulnerability, Threat Intelligence

Meta Description: A security assessment of mobile banking apps from 487 banks found that over half contain critical or high-severity vulnerabilities, including hardcoded secrets.
